subject: Full loop scheduling — Paige Turner: multi-window agenda & panel bridging
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Full loop: Paige Turner — proposed multi-window agenda

Team —

Paige Turner (SWE candidate, backend + infra) confirmed interest in a virtual full loop on Friday 19th. She is East coast (EDT) and prefers morning local time (10am–1pm EDT) or late afternoon (4–6pm EDT). We need to stitch a two-window agenda to accommodate interviewers in PST and a senior infra panel that can only do a 60-minute block.

Proposal (attached: panel-agenda-v1.csv):
- Window A (10:00–12:00 EDT):
  - 10:00–10:30: Systems design (Infra) — Vivek
  - 10:35–11:05: Product/Eng partner — Laura
  - 11:10–11:30: Coding exercise (pairing) — remote

- Midday break + short async take-away for the candidate (15–30m)

- Window B (15:30–17:00 EDT):
  - 15:30–16:00: Culture & leadership — Hiring manager
  - 16:05–16:30: Deep-dive w/serving runtime — Marissa (30m)
  - 16:35–17:00: Final Q&A + wrap

Key asks:
- Vivek: can you confirm 10:00–10:30 for infra? They strictly prefer a compact 30–60 min block; I put them at 30 to keep flow.
- Avery: can you own the debrief and consolidate notes? We should capture the coding task repo link and one prompt set for eval.
- Laura: any blockers from PM side on the 10:35 slot?

If we get a quick thumbs up, I will coordinate with Kate and Paige and send calendar invites. Attaching Paige_Turner_resume.pdf and the CSV agenda.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Recruiting Partner (interview ops)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Paige_Turner_resume.pdf] [Attachment: panel-agenda-v1.csv]
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Full loop: Paige Turner — proposed multi-window agenda

Marissa —

Thanks for the plan. A couple of quick notes:
- PM partner (me) is available at 10:35 but prefer 40 minutes if the candidate is happy — can we extend the product slot to 10:35–11:15 and shorten coding to 20m? That helps cover roadmap discussion.
- Our CS partner (not on thread) may prefer 30m; I can loop them if we finalize.
- Please confirm candidate timezone; if she's EDT we should set invites in EDT to avoid confusion.

If we go 10:35–11:15 for PM, then lunchtime buffer should be 30–45m. I like keeping Vivek's infra early.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Group Product Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Paige Turner — availability for 19 Sep (EDT)

Great — morning it is. Paige, glad morning works. Quick notes on the coding exercise: 20 minutes live pair (we'll ask you to implement a small endpoint and discuss tradeoffs); language is your choice (we typically see Python or Go). We'll send the repo stub before the start of Window A.

Updated agenda attached (panel-agenda-v2.csv) — PM slot extended to 10:35–11:15 as Laura suggested; coding shortened to 11:15–11:35. Break 11:35–12:10. Window B reserved for leadership + final wrap (15:30–17:00 EDT) for interviewers who can only do afternoon.

I've created tentative calendar invites — please accept when you get them: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood_onsite_paige_20250919

Avery — can you own the debrief and confirm you will consolidate notes and send a candidate summary within 24h? Vivek — please confirm infra at 10:00–10:30.

Thanks all,
Marissa

[Attachment: panel-agenda-v2.csv]
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-09-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Full loop scheduling — Paige Turner

Marissa —

I can do 10:00–10:30 PDT (which is 13:00–13:30 EDT) — wait, that conversion is off, sorry. I'm in PST: 10:00–10:30 PDT equals 13:00–13:30 EDT; that's outside the morning window you have. I meant to confirm the 10:00–10:30 EDT slot — my morning is flexible that day; I can make 07:00–07:30 PDT (10:00–10:30 EDT) if scheduled. So yes, I confirm the early infra block at 10:00–10:30 EDT.

One small ask: can we flip the order and do infra first then product so the candidate goes from systems context into product? I think the flow will help technical signal. Otherwise I'm fine.

Vivek
Senior Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
